review: One of the all time great roguelikes, should get as much attention as Binding of Isaac, Slay the Spire, and Hades. A lack of meta-progression keeps it from being quite as addictive as those three, but the core loop is fantastic, and better for not having meta-progression. Lots of interacting systems that lead to nifty learning points and lots of cruel deaths. Fantastic.

Un rogelike único en su categoría, dada la complejidad de sus mecánicas y lo caótico de sus eventos. En un juego medianamente frenético, las constantes probadas de muertes injustas son precisamente las que te obligan a aprender a calcular minuciosamente la consecuencia de tus actos en un mundo impredecible. A diferencia de otros título, la runs no se ven determinadas por la suerte en los objetos que encuentras, y cada victoria se sienten como una recompensa al esfuerzo.

Spelunky 2 is a worthy successor to Spelunky HD. It is vibrant and inspired, being just different enough to feel fresh and but not too much as to be strange and uncanny. But as the serial complainer as I am, there's always a downside. The Dwellings, the concentration of hazards that can instantly end a run, and the variation in quality of new content simply hold this sequel from reaching the sheer high of Spelunky HD.

I hate the Dwellings with a passion. No prizes for guessing two key reasons why. Beyond the obvious, I hate that it conceals the wondrous and wacky environments which lie beyond with its reddish "eugh"-iness and pure testes-in-a-garlic-crusher experience. While perhaps an intentional skill check, it always outlasts my patience for absolute gardening twaddle (in lieu of other strong words) and shamefully turns me towards the 1-4 shortcut almost without fail. And I say this as somebody who was comitted to ironman in Spelunky HD, and very rarely used shortcuts at all.

Other levels also feel uninspired and aesthetically lacking, like filler content. Going from the Jungles to Tide Pool is the difference between a landlord's favourite shade of beige and a nice and tart scarlet. Levels that have brilliant art in the journal have no such detail in actuality, which is quite dismaying because they evidence no lack of ideas, they simply weren't implemented. Volcana and the Jungles could absolutely do with a glow up.

I would also argue that there are far too many things which can insta-kill the player. Nobody likes their run ending suddenly to something they don't have any hope of surviving, especially when these dangers are difficult to spot or are very difficult to avoid. They're manageable with some experience and a seed that isn't comparable to excrement, but ultimately still too common, especially in levels that are tight and winding.

A lesser issue but one that I lament is the soundtrack. Spelunky 2 is one of the few games I prefer to play with the music turned off or extremely low because I simply don't like it. While HD had some solid grooves and a good bit of variance, Spelunky 2 hasn't had anything that's caught my ears or which doesn't become stale after four whole levels with it.

Regardless of my criticism, Spelunky 2 is a good game which should be ample enough for newcomer and veteran alike. It looks fine, it plays fine, and it has more than enough to chew on for the time being. When I have many more hours, I might revisit this review to amend or add something. Who knows.

I've loved Spelunky HD when it released on Xbox 360/Xbox Live Arcade. It's a brutal, fast paced platforming arcade/score attack action with a mostly fair difficulty (there are times where off screen projectiles can completely end your run). And it's sequel is more of the same but cranked up in enemy variety and stage hazards. Strangely, at least in my experience, the rng can vary widely with some very generous/mild runs or the absolute trenches of hell with resources and enemy count/placement, but that's just goes for randomly generated stages in general. Frankly it just happens. Co-op is fun with friends too (can be frustrating with friendly fire, but honestly I think it should be taken as light fun than anything serious). Overall, I still prefer Spelunky HD, which could just be the familiarity/nostalgia talking (and liking the soundtrack more); however, Spelunky 2 is still a great sequel to the series.
